name: Gorrlon
body:
Gorrlon
CR 11

This creature is tall, lanky, hunched and boasts an oversized head. Its perceived danger grows when you notice cords of lean muscle moving under the bronze, reptilian skin. The creature hisses, baring its teeth and looks upon you with a predatory gaze.

XP 12,800
N Large monstrous humanoid
Init +4; Senses darkvision 120 ft., scent; Perception +29

DEFENSE

AC 25, touch 13, flat-footed 21 (+4 Dex, +12 natural, –1 size)
hp 149 (13d10+78)
Fort +10, Ref +12, Will +13
Immune poison; SR 22

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee mwk double glaive +22/+22/+17/+17/+12/+12 (2d6+8/19-20/x3 plus poison), bite +15 (1d8+4), 2 tail slaps +15 (1d8+4) Ranged javelin +16 (1d8+8) or net +16 ranged touch (entangle)
Special Attacks studied target +3 (3rd, swift action)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.

STATISTICS

Str 27, Dex 19, Con 22, Int 13, Wis 20, Cha 8
Base Atk +13; CMB +22; CMD 36
Feats Double Slice, Greater Two-Weapon Fighting, Harvest Parts, Improved Critical (double glaive), Improved Two-Weapon Fighting, Two-Weapon Fighting, Weapon Focus (double glaive)
Skills Craft (taxidermy) +17, Intimidate +15, Perception +29, Stealth +24, Survival +29; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception, +8 Stealth, +8 Survival
Languages Common, Gorrlon
SQ poison savant, hunter’s expertise

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Hunter’s Expertise (Ex)

A gorrlon can attempt knowledge checks to identify creatures, their abilities and weaknesses untrained, adding its Wisdom modifier in addition to its Intelligence modifier to the roll. A gorrlon gains the slayer’s studied target ability, counting its HD as the slayer level.

Poison Savant (Ex)

When a gorrlon applies poison to a weapon, the weapon remains poisoned for a number of hits equal to the gorrlon’s Wisdom modifier (minimum 1, 5 for most gorrlons). A gorrlon is treated as if it had the poison use class feature for the purpose of fulfilling prerequisites. When a gorrlon confirms a critical hit with a poisoned weapon, it increases the save DC of the poison by an amount equal to the weapon’s critical multiplier. A gorrlon often poisons its double glaive before going after dangerous prey. This particular gorrlon uses wyvern poison.

Wyvern Poison—injury; save DC 17; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d4 Constitution damage; cure 2 consecutive saves.

ECOLOGY

Environment any warm
Organization solitary, hunt (1-4 gorrlons plus 1 ranger or slayer of 1st-3rd level), or tribe (9-20; 1-2 rangers or slayers of 1st-3rd level; 1 ranger or slayer of 4th-7th level as leader; 1 shaman of 3rd-5th level)
Treasure double (mwk double glaive, trophy satchel, net, 5 javelins, various trophies and poisons)

Gorrlons are hunters, first and foremost. They spend most of their adolescent and adult lives on their own, hunting increasingly more dangerous prey until, one day, they fail. A great majority of gorrlons live like this, with only the greatest and most venerable hunters becoming semi-settled leaders of the tribe and rare gorrlons with magical aptitude becoming shamans. There is little sexual dimorphism in their species, with males being only slightly larger and stronger than females. The same can be said about gender roles. Females tend to the youngest children and teach them basic skills. There is no traditional family structure, and there is rarely favoritism towards own children from the women of the tribe. Young gorrlons often don’t even know their fathers as their society doesn’t require a relationship between a child and its parents. Except caring for the tribe’s young, female gorrlons are of equal social standing and martial prowess as males, with the latter achieving leadership of the tribe more often only because of slightly better physical characteristics. Children old enough to start going on group hunts remove themselves from any familial bonds and train under the watchful eye of elder hunters until a rite of passage into adulthood, which often occurs even before a gorrlon is fully physically mature. The rite of passage most often consists of finding a poisonous creature, extracting its poison and slaying a dangerous beast with only a poisoned spear. Only after bringing a trophy from such an endeavor does a gorrlon get its double glaive from the tribe’s shaman and starts on his own path.

Gorrlons, despite generally being honorable hunters, are thoroughly fascinated with poison, to which they themselves are immune. Even young gorrlons can readily extract poison from dangerous plants or killed creatures and mix it with such carefully chosen additions that it can form sticky layers on a weapon, being thus usable on multiple strikes. Gorrlons don’t consider using poison dishonorable and instead consider it a staple tool in a hunter’s arsenal. In contrast, they very rarely use ranged weaponry, seeing it as a way of dodging the danger of close quarters combat. Gorrlons sometimes carry weighted javelins as a means of hunting down flying prey, but they prefer throwing nets to bring the flier down to solid ground to dispose of using more direct means. Very rarely, a gorrlon hunter will use a devastating longbow to terrifying effect, though usage of such weaponry against ground-based opponents is forgivable only in self-defense or against targets considered unworthy of melee combat by their own inscrutable measure. The usage of longbows is more common in gorrlons living in mountainous terrain, where flying prey like rocs is prevalent.

Gorrlon society is simple and very loosely knit, but what little tradition they have as a species is quite strong. The first aspect of it are the double glaives, which all gorrlons learn to use with grace and skill hard to match for even elite warriors of other races. While they are hunters first and duelists second, gorrlons relish prey that’s smart enough to figure out it’s being stalked and tough enough to actually stand its ground and pose a challenge. While their culture respects stealth kills, the greatest glory is to be found by cornering your target and defeating it in open combat. The foes that earn the biggest dose of admiration from the hunter, most often by how close they came to kill their pursuer, are then the trophies that the individual gorrlon will cherish the most and will brandish them most eagerly to both kinsmen and as decoration. Important disputes, of leadership and otherwise, are often decided by martial skill and ritual duels, with the victor often killing their opponent. Shamans are a respected caste of gorrlons and while they very rarely assume leadership roles, they are incredibly important in their culture as a whole. While shamans can stand their ground in a fight and most are no slouches in a hunt, their role in the gorrlon society is a different one. They give sage advice on important matters and assist the tribe with their magic, most often healing, but sometimes other types. The shamans are also traditionally craftsmen of double glaives and the only members of gorrlon tribes that can fashion any magical items. The most common of those is the extradimensional trophy satchel that many gorrlons use to carry their gear, trophies and poisons. As for other wondrous equipment, it varies from shaman to shaman, and they are known to create magic weapons and armors, potions and more for the members of their tribe. As gorrlons don’t use money and have barely any concept of trade, the raw materials needed to create those items are gathered in part by the shamans in their spare time, and in part donated by adult gorrlons of the tribe. Every hunter of their species knows not only how to kill almost any given creature, but also has a great sense of what parts of the carcass can be useful not only as trophies, but as materials to the shamans. They carve out parts of bone, sinew, organs and even stranger parts of their victims, keeping them stored safely in their satchels, and every time they return to their homes donate all which aren’t trophies to the shamans, who can make wonders with materials that would make an academically trained wizard craftsman’s head spin. Of course, gorrlons are carnivores and not prone to waste, so much of the carcass that is not predisposed to become either a trophy or a part of the shaman’s new creation is simply eaten.

Gorrlons are surprisingly stealthy for their size and can easily stalk prey undetected in most territories. Their senses are sharp, and their large eyes provide not only superior eyesight but also incredible darkvision, allowing them to hunt at any time of day or night. While their noses and ears are barely visible, their capabilities can easily rival those of almost any beast. By adolescence most gorrlons are skilled enough to easily track even a skilled outdoorsman covering his trail, which is a result of both innate aptitude and extensive training.

The gorrlon language is efficient and consists of various rapid hisses and clicks, often supported by a broad array of gestures. While most gorrlons are capable of understanding and speaking Common, they find it uncomfortable for their mouths, and so only use it if the need is dire, which doesn’t count desperate pleas for parlay screamed out by their unfortunate victims.

An average gorrlon is 11 feet tall and weighs a svelte 900 pounds, their musculature sinewy and bones surprisingly light. Their lizardlike skin is most often bronze in color, but can range from pinkish to gray and even black. Their large hands feature three dexterous digits plus an opposing thumb, and their feet have two large, clawed forward facing toes and a single supporting one extending back from the heel. All gorrlons possess dexterous, split tails which can be used in combat. While gorrlons don’t have much physical variance between relatives, different clans and families often have their specific traits, like expansive birthmarks resembling flowing tattoos or sparse leathery cords growing out of their heads, resembling hair.
